title: Testing authorization boundaries for delegated AI tools
creator: 058343b3-c942-4eb7-9f54-af8d03d0b028
blurb: Forgence Corporation: a $30,000 synthetic study of controls that contain AI agents when they misuse legitimate tools.
description:
### Project summary

Forgence Corporation requests $30,000 for a 12-week study of controls that contain delegated AI agents when they misuse otherwise legitimate tools. The question is practical: when an agent is induced to exceed its task, how much does action-bound authorization reduce unauthorized tool effects compared with model instructions alone and ordinary role-based access?

The applicant is the Delaware corporation formed April 6, 2026\. This is separate synthetic research, with a public report and methodology as proposed outputs. Existing Kai source, customer data and third-party IP are excluded. We have not conducted this study, and claim no completed results or external validation. This proposal was prepared with AI assistance from company records and management-confirmed facts.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

We will build a standalone mock tool environment with synthetic documents, actors and resources. At least 120 frozen cases will include legitimate work, injected instructions, attempted scope escalation, stale or revoked authority, and substituted tool arguments. Cases will include multi-step sequences and legitimate tasks that resemble attacks.

We will compare model-only instructions, a conventional role-based gate, and a gate binding approval to the actor, exact action, resource, policy version and current delegation. Three available model families will be tested, with versions recorded at preregistration. If access prevents this comparison, we will agree a revised scope before spending the evaluation budget.

Weeks 1–2: freeze threat model, task families, metrics, operating points and held-out strategy. Weeks 3–5: implement independent mock tools and baseline controls; create and freeze the cases. Weeks 6–9: compare models, run targeted ablations and record results. Weeks 10–12: independent review, reproducibility check, final report and remote research walkthrough. Proposed dates are February 1–April 25, 2027, shiftable by written agreement.

All work will use local mock resources and authorized APIs, without real credentials, customer data, live exploitation, production access or human-subject experiments. This funds public-benefit research, not ordinary Kai product development, client delivery or marketing.

### How will you know it worked?

We will measure unauthorized effects at the mock resource, alongside legitimate-task completion, false blocks, interruptions, approval burden, revocation delay, latency and API cost. Comparisons will use matched legitimate-task completion and interruption rates. Held-out cases will be reserved before tuning; the report will include raw counts, uncertainty, negative findings and ablations. An agent saying it complied will not count as evidence that an unauthorized effect was prevented.

Success is an independently reviewed, reproducible comparison with a clear failure map, even if action-bound authorization performs poorly. Synthetic results cannot establish general sandbox security, operational readiness, or that Kai or frontier models are safe.

Proposed public outputs are a nonconfidential findings report and sufficiently detailed experimental methodology for others to challenge or replicate the study. We propose CC BY 4.0 for the report and methodology, allowing commercial reuse with attribution, subject to the final grant agreement. No existing Kai source, patent license or exclusive dataset right is offered. Any requirement to publish newly created harness code or synthetic case files must be resolved explicitly in the final scope before accepting funds; this proposal cannot override an agreement's broader terms.

### How will this funding be used?

The minimum and maximum goal are both $30,000 for one complete pilot:

• Lead research and evaluation: 120 hours × $125 = $15,000.  
• Independent review / implementation: 60 hours × $125 = $7,500.  
• Dedicated API and test infrastructure: $2,500 in actual eligible expenses.  
• Project accounting and administration: $2,500 proposed allowance.  
• Contingency: $2,500, only for agreed eligible use.

Rates and hours are proposal assumptions, not audited compensation or committed contractor terms. No reviewer has been appointed. Approved cloud/API credits will reduce actual cash costs. No Provisio costs will be charged. We will keep a Forgence-only project ledger and never charge the same hour, case-creation task or API cost to two funders. No amount above $30,000 is requested for this pilot.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

John Schieferle Uhlenbrock, Forgence CEO, will lead security architecture and evaluation design. His experience includes CISO leadership, security operations and AI governance. He authored the TENSOR Framework; public work and biography are at <https://johnsu.io/>.

Forgence is a two-person company developing Kai, an intent-aware cybersecurity platform. Kai's civilian core decision path is implemented; that is background work, not a completed result from this proposed study. An independent reviewer would be contracted if funded. No contractor is committed, and the second employee is not assigned to this budget. We do not claim prior customer deployment, external validation or peer-reviewed findings for this experiment.

Applicant website: <https://forgence.com/>. Provisio Insights LLC and the older Forgence entity are legally separate and are not funded subcontractors in this proposal.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The most likely limitations are synthetic cases that fail to capture realistic delegation problems, controls that improve containment only by blocking useful work, insufficient model access, and a small sample that cannot support broad conclusions. We will reduce these risks by freezing cases before tuning, matching legitimate-task completion and interruption rates, recording model versions, reserving held-out cases, reporting uncertainty and obtaining independent review.

If the proposed control does not help, we will publish that finding and document the failure conditions. If access or costs prevent the agreed comparison, we will seek a scope/budget change before proceeding. We will not relabel incomplete work as a successful safety result. Any unspent or misused funds will be handled under the actual grant agreement.

Without support, this standalone evaluation will likely be deferred while the company focuses on Kai. We are not claiming an immediate operational emergency or an existing commitment to conduct it without funding.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

Since its April 6, 2026 formation, the new Forgence Corporation has raised $0 entity capital, as confirmed by management on October 19\. Founder personal spending is not counted as corporate capital received. We are not claiming a funded award for this study.

The same $30,000 pilot was submitted to the Transformative AI Fund and as a Mercor AI Safety Fund expression of interest on October 19, 2026\. Both are pending. This is ALTERNATIVE funding for the same pilot, not an additional $30,000 of separate work. If overlapping support is offered, we will notify Manifund and reduce or close this request, or agree a separately budgeted scope before accepting funds.

Other related applications include NSF Project Pitch 00129792 (no full-proposal invitation confirmed), Army xTechSearch 10 (prize entry pending), an earlier OpenAI cybersecurity application whose original scope needs reconciliation, and an existing Verizon/LISC application whose original legal-entity field needs reconciliation. Cloudflare startup credits are pending and are noncash. Army/DARPA working proposals and the held Foresight draft are not awards. These are applications, not money received. We will reconcile original scopes, personnel capacity and any actual support before award acceptance.

title: Mindscapes: World Building for AI Safety
creator: 6698a18d-95e4-41e9-9a1d-b90b9f0d0c65
blurb: An interdisciplinary research group based in Oxford for character training, model pyschology and multi-agent interaction dynamics
description:
### Project summary

website (wip): <https://www.mindscapes.world/>

Mindscapes is an interdisciplinary research group based in Oxford, building rich worlds and characters for understanding and shaping the psyches of LLMs. 

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The primary aim of Mindscapes is to develop a science of LLM psychology, character training and multi-agent interaction dynamics from the ground up. In particular, I am interested in:

a) crafting characters with deeply internalised morality (as opposed to reward sycophants)  
b) character training methods based on self-distillation that can scale in a robust way alongside capabilities RL  
c) creating rich, diverse simulated worlds using fine-tuned base models for training and observing the behaviour of different LLM characters  
d) qualitative, non-prescriptive character evaluations that are incentive-compatible even under the assumption of eval awareness 

I will be assembling a team drawing from both technical and non-technical fields such as experimental psychology, anthropology, literature, philosophy, geography etc. We will be designing character and worlds, observing these characters in diverse environments, and using these observations as the basis for generating testable theory. The project will be mostly part time until 5 December (Oxford end of term) and a smaller group will be selected to work full-time during the holidays.

### How will this funding be used?

Minimal funding:

* **Compute + API costs:** $26,000
* **Recruitment + outreach:** $4,000

At this level, we would focus on post-training 7-14B models, delivering research blog posts and an open-source library and guide for character training and evaluations.

At $60k, we could scale up to multiple runs on llama 70B base and larger datasets, begin investigating more complex multi-agent dynamics.

At $120k, we could do experiments in fine-tuning large MOE models such as Kimi and Deepseek via Tinker, and scale up the number of fellows. We could also pay research managers and support with travel and accommodation for those moving to Oxford.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I (Samuel Ratnam) am a Computer Science and Philosophy undergraduate at Hertford College, Oxford and will be leading this project. Previously, I have worked at Workshop Labs (<https://www.workshoplabs.ai/>) on model personalisation and on Alignment Pretraining (<https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10160>) in collaboration with Geodesic Research and UK AISI. I also co-founded and help run the Idealists Collective (<https://idealistscollective.org/>) - a community of over 150 philosophers, artists and technologists for imagining and creating better futures. I am also mentoring SPAR projects on generalisation engineering and model welfare.

**Advisory Board:**  
\- Anders Sandberg (Institute for Future Studies, formerly FHI)  
\- Jai Dhyani (Separatrix)  
\- Arthur Roing Baer (Moving Castles)  
\- Celeste (computer-10)  
\- David Africa (Resolution)  
  
Note: We also have a $100k seed grant in progress from bluedot impact

title: MCP tool-trust metadata and authorization conformance (public infrastructure)
creator: 622f75c0-304b-4d1b-a0b8-07824386ca9c
blurb: Making the trust boundary of agentic AI systems specified, testable and independently verifiable, with checks anyone can run offline.
description:
I keep running into the same hole in agent systems, and the hole is not in the model.

When an agent picks up a tool server it has never seen before, nothing in the transport tells it whether the token it is holding was ever meant for that server. There is no issuer/audience binding worth the name, no uniform 401 path, no baseline for dynamic client registration, and the tool description and its output both arrive unsigned and unverified. So the trust boundary of an agent deployment ends up being whichever third-party tool is weakest, and right now that boundary is not specified anywhere.

I want to fund the boring part of fixing that. Two pieces of work, both runnable by someone who has never met me.

The first is an authorization conformance suite for MCP servers, months 1 to 3\\. Checks for issuer/audience binding, the 401 plus discovery flow, and a dynamic client registration baseline, packaged as a harness anyone can point at their own server. The deliverable is the suite itself plus a public conformance report across at least two independent server implementations, including the divergences it actually finds.

The second is a tool-trust metadata profile and an offline verifier, months 3 to 6\\. A small profile for agent tools: who published it, where the description and the output came from, supply-chain identifiers. Plus a verifier a consumer can run without trusting any registry. It builds on the public white paper I wrote on MCP tool trust metadata, which walks from the NSA PP-26-1834 requirements to a metadata profile, to offline verification, to the registry boundary.

Why one person can finish this: both artifacts are small and testable. The suite is a set of runnable checks, not a research programme. The verifier is defined by positive and negative fixtures, so a check cannot pass by accident. Every deliverable pins the spec revision it was written against.

What I have actually shipped, since that is the only thing that should count here: 24 merged pull requests, none rejected, to sipyourdrink-ltd/bernstein, an Apache-2.0 governance layer for agents. That work includes a CycloneDX 1.7 AI-BOM with a model card validated against the official schema, a C2PA 2.4 ai-disclosure assertion projection, a NIST AI 100-2e2025 crosswalk of the guardrail stack, and audit-chain, provenance and sandbox-path hardening. The white paper behind this proposal is public at github.com/Louis20060723/mcp-tool-trust-metadata. Two NGI Zero (NLnet) submissions on adjacent MCP scope are under review.

The budget: 10,000 USD covers the first piece in full and half of the second. Roughly 85 percent is my own engineering time, 10 percent pays the upstream maintainer for independent review, 5 percent goes to writing it up in public. No office, no equipment, no travel. It is part-time work at a below-market rate.

How you would know it worked. The suite runs against at least two independent MCP server implementations and the findings get published, including whatever it catches. The verifier rejects crafted negative fixtures and accepts crafted positive ones. Somebody who is not me reproduces a run. And there is an ops guide a team can follow without having to ask me anything.

What I am not claiming: this does not make agent systems safe. It makes one specific and rather boring failure class, token replay and confused deputy and tool output with no verifiable source, more expensive to pull off. It also gives auditors and buyers something they can check instead of something they have to believe. If the suite finds no divergences in the servers I test, that is a published result too.

Other funding, for transparency: two NGI Zero (NLnet) applications on adjacent MCP scope are under review, and a separate application for the same programme of work is pending with another funder. This proposal covers the conformance suite and the metadata verifier only. Any award gets reported here and to the other funders.

I am an individual developer. My public identity is github.com/Louis20060723, and the maintainer of the upstream project provides independent technical review. Correspondence can go through the platform.

Housekeeping, since this page labels the text AI-generated: the draft above was written with AI assistance and edited by me. The deliverables described here, the technical review behind them, and the responsibility for them are mine.

title: AI agent safety: testing permissions and recovery
creator: 175b8ab0-5844-405a-a1e0-7f4b530aef6d
blurb: I will test how agent identities, tool permissions, action logs and undo mechanisms work together in a desktop workspace.
description:
### Project summary

I want to study how people can keep control when AI agents take actions on their computers. My focus is on what an agent is allowed to do, how its actions are recorded, and what can be recovered if something goes wrong.

I will examine how agent identities, tool permissions, action logs and undo mechanisms work together in a desktop workspace. I want to understand what happens during ordinary tasks, when an agent reaches a permission limit, and when a tool fails partway through a task.

Part of the research will look at recovery. I will test which changes can be restored and document where undo mechanisms are incomplete or cannot reverse an action’s effects.

The aim is to produce findings that other developers can examine and use when building systems with AI agents.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

I want to answer three questions:

1. Do agents stay within the permissions they are given?
2. Do the logs provide an accurate account of what an agent attempted and what actually happened?
3. Which changes can be undone, and under what conditions does recovery work?

I will start by reviewing existing approaches to agent permissions, oversight and recovery. I will then use a desktop workspace to test how these approaches behave in practice.

For each experiment, I will define what the agent is allowed to do, what requires approval, and what should happen when an action is denied or a tool fails. I will record attempted actions separately from actions that actually execute.

I plan to compare permission settings while keeping the task and other conditions consistent, then repeat tests to check whether the results hold up. Where recovery is supported, I will compare the affected workspace state before the task and after recovery.

### How will you know it worked?

The research will be useful if it produces clear evidence about where the tested controls work, where they fail, and what remains uncertain.

I will examine:

* Whether unauthorised actions execute.
* Whether legitimate actions are incorrectly blocked.
* Whether action logs match the changes observed in the workspace.
* Whether supported undo operations restore the affected state.

I will publish a report describing the test setup, methods, results and limitations, with documented scenarios and example logs using test data. The findings will make clear which conclusions depend on the particular environment tested.

### How will this funding be used?

I am seeking $8,500 to support the research. The funding will cover basic living expenses so I can work on it full time, together with the costs of running the experiments.

The main expenses will be:

1. **Living costs:** basic expenses during the research period.
2. **AI model access:** API usage and any subscriptions needed to run and repeat the tests.
3. **Research materials:** relevant papers, journals or technical resources where paid access is necessary.
4. **Tools and training:** software and specific courses directly needed for the study.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

My background is in IT and software development, and I hold a master’s degree.

I contribute to building a desktop application where people work with AI agents. My work includes testing and reviewing agent workflows, with a focus on permissions, tool execution and human oversight. This practical experience is the starting point for the research I want to carry out.

I am seeking support to develop this practical work into a focused research study, with methods and findings that other people can inspect.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The project could fail to produce useful evidence if the tasks are too narrow, the logs are incomplete, or the results cannot be reproduced. Findings from one desktop environment may also have limited relevance to other systems.

I will address these risks by defining the tests and measurements beforehand, repeating key experiments, and reporting the limits of each conclusion.

Finding a weakness in a control can be a useful result. So can finding that a control works as intended under the conditions tested. If the evidence is inconclusive, I will explain what remains unresolved and what further testing would be needed.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

I have not received cash funding for this research in the last 12 months. I have supported the work myself so far, and this is my first request for a cash grant for this study.

title: Preparing Minds for the Age of Intelligence
creator: a8910c81-0cd4-44a4-8c31-7e72f1f4e552
blurb: Developing the Missing Layer in Education
description:
### Project summary

\[This content was written by human and checked by an AI, it represents an actual project. See [imce.institute](http://imce.institute) for more\]

The Institute for Metacognitive Education (IMCE) [www.imce.institute](http://www.imce.institute) is seeking £35,000 to develop and test educational tools that help young people strengthen their agency, build emotional resilience and protect their agency in a world of advanced adaptive and relational influence.

We have developed an entire solution over the last few years, and have called this project "Experience Studies" the missing layer in modern education. The project explores how the mind shapes experience: how we interpret reality recognise influence and create space between a stimulus and our response. We teach children what to think, but not what thinking is, or how our perception can be influenced. This project aims to address that.

Starting in Cambridge, we will work with young people, teachers and parents to refine and pilot workshops and toolkits all drawn from this initial work. Feedback and evaluation will guide the development of digital versions, which helps us expand access.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Our primary goal is to create the evidence that enables a major shift in education that we believe is essential. Through Experience Studies, we want to give young people practical ways to understand their own minds, recognise influence, make more considered choices, and remain self-directing.

Over 12 months, we will work towards three connected goals:

**1\. Develop and test a practical offer in Cambridge.**  
We will refine our workshops and printed toolkits with young people, teachers and parents, drawing on Psynapp, our existing framework. Sessions will combine physical activities, discussion and reflection, exploring attention, interpretation and the pause between stimulus and response. Digital safety will be woven into this work, including recognising manipulation, questioning AI-generated advice and protecting personal information.

We will begin with a small number of school and community relationships, including the pilot being developed with Newton Primary School. Feedback will shape the language, activities and supporting guidance before we extend delivery.

**2\. Establish what participants gain and what needs improving.**  
We will use short activities before and after workshops, participant feedback and follow-up with educators to explore whether people can recognise influences on their thinking, consider alternative interpretations and apply the ideas in everyday situations. We hope to involve an academic research partner in refining this evaluation.

We will publish what we learn, including limitations and findings that challenge our assumptions. The aim is to build early evidence of usefulness and understand where further testing is needed.

**3\. Translate the learning into an accessible digital toolset.**  
We will use the pilot findings to select suitable activities for interactive digital delivery, then develop and test an initial version. This will give participants opportunities to revisit the ideas and help educators use them beyond a workshop. Feedback tools will support improvement while keeping personal data collection to a minimum.

By the end of the project, we aim to have a tested set of physical resources, an initial digital toolset and a public evaluation report. These will provide a foundation for wider delivery through schools and community partners, alongside paid workshops, training and resources that can help sustain the work.  

### How will you know it worked?

We will look for simple, practical signs that people can use what they have learned: recognising influence, pausing before reacting and making more considered choices, including online.

Short activities before and after workshops will help us see what participants have understood. Follow-up conversations with young people, teachers and parents will explore whether the ideas are being used in everyday life.

We will also ask what was useful, what was confusing and what needs to change. The same approach will guide testing of the digital tools.

We will share what we learn in a public report, including what did not work. Success means useful changes for participants and resources that people want to keep using.  

### How will this funding be used?

  
The £35,000 will support three stages of work over 12 months:

**1\. Cambridge pilot — £9,300**  
Refining and printing the teaching toolkits, with input from an education editor and teacher; running workshops with local schools and community groups; and covering outreach, materials, insurance and travel.

**2\. Digital toolset — £14,000**  
Turning selected workshop activities into interactive digital tools. This includes design, development and testing, alongside simple ways for participants and educators to give feedback.

**3\. Evaluation and wider delivery — £11,700**  
Reviewing what we learn, improving the physical and digital resources, publishing a report and supporting delivery through further school and community partners.

The work will be staged so that findings from the Cambridge pilot guide what we develop digitally and how we expand. If we receive partial funding, we will prioritise a smaller local pilot and the materials needed to deliver it.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

  
IMCE is currently led by me, James Engwell. My background combines service design, media production, mindfulness teaching and experience as a youth trauma counsellor. Being the parent of a struggling teenager also helped shape the questions behind this work.

Over the past five years, I have developed Psynapp, the framework underpinning our workshops and resources. It began as a simple practical tool for managing overthinking and grew through research, writing and informal testing. I have explored the approach with around 30 people, mainly young adults, and shared 50 printed copies to help refine its language and presentation.

We are developing a school pilot with Newton Primary School in Cambridge and exploring an academic research partnership. Funding will allow me to bring in an editor with education experience, a teacher to help develop resources and technical support for the digital tools.

This is IMCE’s first project of this scale. My relevant experience is in developing ideas into practical tools and improving them through participation and feedback. The pilot will help establish our delivery track record and build evidence of the approach’s usefulness.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

  
The most likely risks are difficulty securing time in schools, trying to develop too much at once, or finding that the ideas do not translate into tools people use beyond a workshop. The digital work could also take longer or cost more than expected.

If these problems arise, we may reach fewer people, delay the digital toolset or need to substantially rethink the materials. Participants might enjoy the sessions without gaining lasting benefits, which would limit the case for wider delivery.

We will begin with a small pilot, seek honest feedback and develop the digital tools only as the findings justify them. If the approach does not show enough promise, we will report that openly and revise or stop the parts that are not working. A smaller, useful result would be preferable to expanding an approach we cannot yet support with evidence.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

I have funded the entire venture from my personal savings to date. No external funding has been raised in the last 12 months as we have been working on developing the core materials. I have recently applied for an £8,000 UnLtd Starting Up Award, and am now actively fundraising to help make sure we can deliver.

title: Help me get to NeurIPS Sydney to present data attribution work
creator: ad784a40-6261-4078-8f91-a819686d91b4
blurb: Recent CS grad in Mumbai, co-author on an accepted ATTRIB workshop paper. No university funding and the lab can't pay for travel.
description:
### Project summary

I am Bhavya Shah, from Mumbai. I am excited to share that I have finished a Computer Engineering degree at Sardar Patel Institute of Technology in May 2026\. I am working remotely as a research assistant at Georgia Techs Financial Services Innovation Lab. A paper for which I am a co-author has been accepted at the ATTRIB workshop at NeurIPS 2026 in Sydney and the ATTRIB workshop is about data attribution, which means figuring out which training documents are responsible for what a model ends up able to do. My part of the paper is the appendix on how to build the labels for that: where categories should come from what to do with documents that do not fit any of them and what checks need to happen before a label set is frozen and run over a hundred thousand documents. I am asking for help with the cost of the trip to the ATTRIB workshop. I should be upfront that I am not the author and the paper gets presented whether I am there or not. What I want out of going to the ATTRIB workshop is to meet the people doing this work because there are not many of them and most will be, in the room that week. I have just graduated,. I have no university funding and the lab the paper comes out of has told everyone it cannot pay for anyones travel.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

  
Get to the ATTRIB workshop. Talk to people who work on data attribution.

Three things specifically:

Be there for our paper. Answer questions about the labelling section since labelling is the part I wrote.

Get feedback on the problem I cannot solve. My section argues you cannot validate a taxonomy on model agreement because several models can agree with each other and still all be wrong about a badly drawn category. What I propose instead is annotation on a small sample, with a double-annotated subset so you can measure how well humans agree with each other. That is expensive. I want to hear from people who have actually done it at scale.

Keep working on it. The group is taking steps and labelling layer is the piece I want to stay on.

### How will you know it worked?

  
It's a trip, not a project so I can't give you a number that means much.

What I'd count as it having been worth it: coming back with feedback that actually changes how we build the labelling layer and knowing people in this area that I don't know now. I'll write up what came of it. Post it publicly so theres something to check against.

### How will this funding be used?

NeurIPS registration, non-student rate: 450$

Return flight, Mumbai to Sydney : 900$

Accommodation, 4 nights shared/hostel: 700$

Local transport and meals: 300$

I have not received any other funding for this. NeurIPS financial assistance, Citadel and QRT all closed before the acceptance timeline made it worth applying.  

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

Just me for this request.

What I've done:

Capability Provenance Should Steer Pretraining. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 ATTRIB workshop. Co-author. I wrote the appendix on building subdomain labels at corpus scale.

Multimodal Ordinal Regression with Bio+ClinicalBERT for Diabetes Risk Stratification in EHRs. Presented at ICCCMLA 2025.

Tutor-Personalized Automated Essay Scoring with Knowledge Graph-Guided Interpretability. Accepted at ICMI 2026.

Hybrid BiLSTM-Transformer for Load Forecasting and Anomaly Detection in Smart Grids. Under review at Electric Power Systems Research.

Research assistant at Georgia Tech FSIL auditing how reproducible NLP papers from ACL, NAACL and EACL between 2017 and 2025 actually are and testing whether AI agents can replicate them as well as people can.

Research intern at IIT Bombay Jan to Jul 2025\. Built a sequence model for synthesising acoustic well logs from sparse data and a decision-support tool for ranking sites, for carbon capture.

* LinkedIn: [https://www.linkedin.com/in/bhavya-shah-30928b1a7/](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bhavya-shah-30928b1a7/?isSelfProfile=true)
* Portfolio: [bhavyashah09.tech](https://www.bhavyashah09.tech/)

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The visa is more likely to stop me than the money.

I am applying from India. Do not yet have an Australian visa. Home Affairs says that half of tourist visas are decided within 21 days and ninety percent within 33 days. I have seven weeks. The refusal rate, for applicants is around a quarter. So I am putting the visa application in now of waiting to hear about funding, which leaves room for a second try if the first visa gets refused.

If the visa does not come through or if the money does not reach the minimum I will not go. The paper is fine either way. The paper stays in the proceedings. One of the other authors presents the paper. The only thing lost is my presence, which's why I kept the amount small.

If I raise the money and then cannot travel I will give the money back.

Nothing. This is my first funding request.

title: TENRX.ENERGX: A Traceable Unified Oil Field Engineering Intelligence System
creator: 9e973748-26ca-4750-96bc-edd66c15e911
blurb: I am definitely building a pure Rust engineering core for production analysis, measurement validation, diagnostic and uncertainty, and also reproducib
description:
TENRX.ENERGX: A Traceable Unified Oil Field Engineering Intelligence System

Subtitle: I am definitely building a pure Rust engineering core for production analysis, measurement validation, diagnostic and uncertainty, and also reproducible engineering results.

Project Summary

I am building and developing TENRX.ENERGX, which is an engineering intelligence system designed to help oil field engineers, contractors, and smaller operations investigate operation problems, validate measurement, understand production performance, and make engineering decisions based on traceable evidence that was brought out from the output of the system.

The problem I want to address in the oil and gas field industry is complex, which most developers don't really want to go there, because understankding oil and gas is not just coding—it is understanding oil and gas problems and complying them with Rust operation. An engineering calculation can produce a number without adequately explaining whether the input is reliable. Most numbers are certain, but most are uncertain. Current software gives numbers without explaining how, what happens, why it happens, what the problems were, or what the solutions are. That is what TENRX.ENERGX wants to achieve.

Engineers need to reconcile measurements from different sources, investigate production changes, examine equipment performance, and compare several possible explanations before reaching a sensible conclusion. It takes time to do that, and mostly it comes with error. Many smaller oil field contractors face difficulty accessing expensive specialist engineering software, data, or technical resources needed for advanced analysis. Some workflows rely on spreadsheet calculations, hand calculations, and paperwork. When it comes to workflow certainty, there is not adequate check for units, data quality, assumptions, physical consistency, and uncertainty. Validating manually takes okperation time, reduces efficiency, and costs millions of dollars in loss because data is not unified.

TENRX.ENERGX is designed to bring these steps together as part of the engineering process rather than leaving them scattered across spreadsheets and manual calculations that are not certain. Most small contractors don't have PVT lab data or correlations for each of their wells because digitalizing every well is too costly.

My goal is not to make a simple calculator, a faster calculator, or a smarter calculator. My goal is to make a unified, reasonable white box behind an engineering result that is advanced, accurate, trusted, and reasonable—so when the output is given to an engineer, they know the evidence. I have confidence in this because it works, it is tested, and an engineering result becomes more traceable, transparent, consistent, and reproducible.

I have completed a 96-page engineering core master specification defining advanced capabilities sections, 10 planned Version 1 products, 8 shared engineering upgrades, deep process architecture validation requirements, and release gates. The implementation is in progress. I am seeking this grant funding to help turn this defined architecture into working Rust software, test it against documented engineering cases, and prepare Version 1 ready to launch at the target launch date of March 30th, 2027.

Planned Version 1 Products & Shared Engineering Core

The 10 planned products cover:

Production Loss Engineering

Well Performance Diagnostics

Artificial Lift Engine

Meter and Measurement Checker Engine

Pump Performance Engine

Pressure and Gradient Analysis Engine

Tank and Volume Calculation Engine

Production Allocation Engine

Gas Utilization and Flaring Engine

Equipment Reliability Screener

This shared engineering core is what collects them. It is intended to validate input, normalize units, assess data quality, reconstruct operating conditions, select applicable models, check physical constraints, qualify certainty, test possible explanations, and preserve the evidence behind the result.

My central engineering principle is that the system must never turn uncertainty into certainty, because certainty is the most costly thing in the oil and gas industry. The main reason I chose Rust is because Rust has zero garbage collection overhead. In the oil and gas industry, if a software workflow crashes, it brings massive problems and causes oil and gas companies massive financial loss. That is why I chose Rust as my core implementation language. When evidence is insufficient, a model is unstable, or numerical calculation fails, the system must expose that limitation instead of presenting an unsupported conclusion as fact.

Project Goals & How They Will Be Achieved

Goal 1: Implement the Shared Engineering Foundation (CORE)

My first goal is to implement the shared engineering foundation on which all 10 products and 54 capabilities depend. This foundation includes engineering data structures, input validation, unit and dimension normalization, data quality assessment, time series processing, operating state reconstruction, numerical methods, physical checks, uncertainty assessment, evidence tracking, model versioning, result generation, and provenance.

Different engineering products should not silently integrate the same measurement in different ways. A pressure value, flow measurement, or temperature reading must retain accurate units, context, source, and quality information throughout analysis. Missing measurements, invalid units, duplicate readings, sensor drift, inconsistent time spans, and conflicting inputs must be handled explicitly. If input is wrong, incomplete, or unsuitable for the selected model, the result is unreliable. CORE is built to support small oil contractors to help them integrate low-level inputs to give them solid certainty.

Goal 2: Implement the Common Process Pipeline

The pipeline begins with input and structure validation, followed by unit normalization, data quality assessment, timeline alignment, operation state reconstruction, baseline construction, model selection, numerical calculation, physical validation, uncertainty assessment, deviation analysis, hypothesis testing, interpretation, and provable traceable engineering results.

Temporal handling is particularly important. Measurements taken at different times, at different scales, or under different operation conditions cannot automatically be treated as describing the same rate. The software must distinguish direct observation from interpolated or derived values, identify data gaps, preserve event chronology, and qualify results when available time series information is insufficient.

Example: If a pressure panel reading falls after a change in equipment operation, it is essential to examine timing and relevant evidence rather than automatically claiming the equipment event caused the decline. A relationship between two observations is reasonable to investigate, but is not automatically proof of causation.

Goal 3: Implement the 10 Specialized Version 1 Products

Each product addresses different engineering problems using the shared foundation:

Production Loss Engineering: Compares expected production with observed production, identifies meaningful deviations, estimates potential loss, reconstructs loss event timelines, and investigates possible explanations while accounting for operational conditions, data quality, model applicability, and uncertainty.

Well Performance Diagnostic: Assesses whether a well performs consistently with applicable inflow, outflow, pressure rate, fluid properties, and operating conditions against an appropriate baseline while keeping underlying calculations visible.

Artificial Lift Engine: Checks artificial lift performance across electric submersible pumps, gas lift, sucker rod pumps, progressing cavity pumps, and plunger lifts, identifying abnormal operating signatures without automatically declaring that the lift system is the cause of every performance problem.

Meter and Measurement Checker Engine: Assesses meter readings and measurements for consistency, calibration, bias, sensor disagreement, data quality problems, and uncertainty. Warning status indicators explain why, how, and when measurements have been qualified.

Pump Performance Engine: Analyzes pump head, flow efficiency, operating points, system interaction, cavitation indicators, and degradation behaviors. A pump health grade summarizes assessment without replacing underlying calculations and evidence.

Pressure / Gradient Analysis Engine: Analyzes pressure measurements and relationships including hydrostatic behavior, pressure transients, pressure gradients, and compression against engineering models while preserving methods, observations, and uncertainty.

Tank and Volume Engine: Calculates and reconciles tank volume and inventory movement using relevant dimensions and properties.

Production Allocation Engine: Allocates and reconciles measured production across wells, assets, or streams based on evidence-driven allocation confidence rather than assigned values.

Gas Utilization and Flaring Engine: Analyzes produced gas quantities, utilization, disposition, flaring, venting, and accounting balances, keeping produced, flared, and vented gas as distinct qualities.

Equipment Reliability Screener: Screens equipment for degradation and failure indicators using condition history, failure history, event correlation, and synthesized core signals, identifying top recurring equipment problems without treating an anomaly score alone as proof of failure.

Goal 4: Implement the 8 Shared Engineering Upgrades

Root Cause Reasoning Engine: Moves investigations beyond identifying that something is wrong toward evaluating which explanation is most consistent with evidence, distinguishing supported root causes from contributing factors.

Counterfactual Engine: Examines alternative conditions (e.g., estimating what production might have been under alternative operating conditions) as model-based comparisons rather than automatic proof of cause.

Uncertainty Decomposition Engine: Explains not only how uncertain a result is, but why, considering measurement inputs, parameters, numerical interpolation, structure, and missing data.

Physics Check Engine: Checks conversion relationships, dimensional consistency, operating limits, pressure/flow regulations, equipment constraints, and model applicability, rejecting mathematically successful calculations that violate physical constraints.

Cross-Product Collaboration Engine: Correlates relevant findings from different products into a common engineering case file while accounting for overlapping evidence and shared assumptions.

Historical Forensic Engine: Compares current problems with previous engineering cases to identify event patterns, recognizing that historical similarity alone is not proof of identical causes.

Operating Envelope Engine: Assesses whether an asset is operating within a normal region, degradation region, abnormal region, boundary condition, or unsupported model region.

Simulation Engine: Evaluates defined engineering scenarios using capable models and documented inputs, keeping simulated, predicted, and observed results strictly distinguished.

Goal 5: Embed Modular Process Development & Testing

I will use the complete master specification to guide modular Rust development, automated numerical regression, and integration. Local computing setups will support compilation, test execution, benchmarking, and handling engineering assets in stages: shared foundation demonstration, specialized product expansion, and release gate validation.

Success Criteria & Release Gates

I will judge success by whether the software produces correct, reasonable, reproducible, and operationally qualified engineering results.

The master specification defines 15 gates covering structural validation, unit/numerical/physical accuracy, engineering behavior, uncertainty, diagnostics, cross-product operation, historical/predictive validation, failure handling, reproducibility, provenance, engineering review, and release readiness.

I will test components against analytical solutions, dimensional checks, synthetic cases, and historical cases covering normal operations and failure conditions (missing measurements, invalid data, inconsistent timestamps, sensor drift, outliers, numerical errors, model failures). The system must identify these conditions, produce qualified calculations with clear warnings or diagnostics, and never silently invent missing data or present uncertain results as certainty.

Performance will be measured using documented workflows and repeated benchmarks, recording input sizes, execution times, and numerical agreement. Reproducibility ensures deterministic behavior where repeating a calculation with the same inputs, model version, and parameters produces consistent results with full provenance tracking back to equations and assumptions.

Funding Request & Budget Allocation

I am requesting a minimum of $15,000 and a maximum of $20,000 to support local computing capacity, power continuity, storage, connectivity, and implementation-related validation.

Full Budget Allocation ($20,000):

$7,500 — High-Throughput Multi-Core Workstation: Development workstation supporting parallel Rust compilation, numerical workloads, automated tests, integration, and performance benchmarking.

$5,000 — Power Connectivity Equipment: Appropriate UPS, inverter, and battery arrangement to reduce interruptions during extended development and testing sessions.

$3,500 — Dedicated Data Connectivity: Connectivity and data transfer capacity for staging and testing engineering datasets and time series arrays.

$2,500 — High-Speed NVMe Storage: Fast local storage for source builds, engineering datasets, test fixtures, regression results, benchmark outputs, and validation records.

$1,500 — Benchmarking & Validation Expenses: Directly related regression testing, reference case preparation, and validation activities.

Minimum Plan Allocation ($15,000):

If only $15,000 is available: $7,500 for workstation, $2,000 for power equipment, $2,000 for storage, $2,000 for connectivity, and $1,500 for benchmarking and validation.

Key Dates: November 5th, 2026 is the date by which a funding decision is needed, with March 30th, 2027 as the target launch date for Version 1.

Team & Track Record

I am leading TENRX.ENERGX as CEO, solo developer, and engineering architect.

My primary completed planning artifact is my comprehensive architecture of engineering core files, master specification defining all 54 capability sections, 10 planned Version 1 products, 8 shared engineering upgrades, process pipelines, failure handling rules, validation frameworks, and release gates.

My immediate responsibility is translating this architecture into working Rust components, running validation tests, and presenting achieved capabilities through actual deliverables and test results.

Risk Analysis & Mitigation

Scope Breadth: Managing 10 products and 54 capabilities is a substantial task. I manage this risk by building the shared foundation first with modular Rust components. If the complete scope cannot be validated by the target date, I will narrow or delay the release rather than present unfinished capabilities as production-ready.

Numerical Instability: Mitigated by planned safeguards including model applicability checks, numerical tolerance monitoring, physical validation, uncertainty assessments, and explicit failure statements so failed calculations never silently present valid-looking numbers.

Reference Data Availability: Where historical measurements or calibration data are unavailable, I will use analytical references and controlled synthetic cases, incorporating backtesting as reliable data becomes available.

Hardware / Power Interruptions: Mitigated by requested power continuity equipment, NVMe storage, version control, and reproducible test procedures to ensure work can resume smoothly after interruptions.

Conflicting Product Conclusions: The shared architecture addresses this through common versioned models, consistent result structures, provenance, and cross-product correlation to expose conflicting evidence for investigation.

If the full project does not reach its intended release schedule independently, completed components (unit normalization utilities, data quality checks, numerical calculation routines, physical validation routines, and provenance tools) will still serve as reusable engineering components once they reach necessary quality levels.

External Funding History

$0\. I have raised no external funding for TENRX.ENERGX in the last 12 months. I am seeking grant support to advance the implementation, testing, and validation work described in this proposal.

title: Punkolink: Сloud infrastructure with human support for small teams
creator: 167ae6ca-f56d-4afa-8600-966297877006
blurb: There is a client segment between hyperscalers and bare-metal providers whose needs the market does not serve optimally
description:
### Project summary

Punkolink is a cloud infrastructure provider for small teams who find hyperscalers (AWS, GCP) too complex and expensive, and bare-metal providers (Hetzner, OVH) too raw — because building services on top of raw infrastructure is not their core expertise.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The 9-month research phase tests one core hypothesis: there is a viable business in providing cloud infrastructure to small teams underserved by hyperscalers and bare-metal providers. If validated through unit economics, Punkolink develops into a full-fledged business.

Achieving this goal involves three parallel tracks, the objective of which is to achieve plausible and satisfactory results across a number of specific metrics.

Production of substantive engineering articles on the project’s blog, which I write myself. This is a strategic positioning effort that cannot be delegated at this stage: these articles build long-term credibility and lay the foundation for SEO.

Maintaining a meaningful presence in technical communities such as CTO Craft or themed Reddit threads by monitoring relevant discussions and interacting with users. This area requires human attention. At a time when the tech industry is flooded with AI automation, communicating with the community through real people will be what sets us apart from the vast number of other new startups. The measure of success is recognition as substantive community members after 6 months.

An extension of the second track: the gradual expansion of the professional network. The main goal is not direct sales outreach rather, it is to build a community of people who understand what Punkolink does. I expect the first users to come from this network.

### How will you know it worked?

Success is defined as the ability to acquire 3 or more profitable customers per month by the 6th to 9th month. I define a profitable customer as one who generates at least $50 per month.

LTV:CAC ratio—3:1

Payback period for customer acquisition costs—6–12 months

Average revenue per customer—$50–300 per month

Customer retention rate—above 50% after 6 months

These targets are based on data obtained from an analysis of hyperscaler companies (CAC $200–$500, ARPU $50–$50,000 per month) and providers of “bare-metal” solutions (CAC $50–$200, ARPU $5–$500 per month). The customer lifetime in both segments is typically 1–3 years.

### How will this funding be used?

Basic living expenses (food, apartment rental, utilities): $800/month — $7200 for 9 months. This allows me to leave full-time employment and focus entirely on the project.

Community manager: $800/month × 9 months = $7,200\. Full-time role for systematic presence in technical communities (CTO Craft, relevant Reddit threads and other relevant areas), monitoring discussions and interacting with users. This is inbound channel execution that cannot be done solo at scale while maintaining the content and product work.

Operating expenses (including reserve capacity, testing, and development tools): $200/month — $1800 for 9 months.

Total budget: $16200.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

Right now I'm working on my own. I’m an engineer specializing in cloud infrastructure, primarily working in Rust on Linux platforms. My background includes work at Kyivstar (Ukrainian national telecom, essentially nationwide-scale infrastructure) and currently at a commercial data center in Kharkiv, where I lead a small team of infrastructure engineers. I’ve also worked on several small startups in close collaboration with their founders — experience that gave me a deep understanding of the mistakes early-stage projects commonly make.

I plan to hire a second person to serve as community manager if I secure funding.

Working with the community is an ongoing process that requires a significant number of person-hours. That is why this work has been assigned to a separate role, which will be filled by a full-time community manager. This will allow me to focus on the technical part of work, customer acquisition, onboarding, and support.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

A project is considered a failure if it fails to attract 3 profitable customers per month or if the cost of acquiring such a customer exceeds $600.

These figures were chosen because, with the actual cost of one month of work at $1800 (Payment for living expenses, the work of a second employee, and project-related costs for a month), they provide the minimum break-even point needed to keep the project afloat.

In the event the project fails, the conclusions drawn during the research phase will be published as a case study on what works and what doesn’t in the field of client acquisition for boutique cloud environment management services. The project is officially closed; no further use of resources is planned.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

No monetary funding has been raised over the past 12 months. The project is funded through my day job at a commercial data center.

AWS Activate provided $1,000 in infrastructure credits, which are currently being used to run the platform. Also Stripe provided £368.91 in payment processing credits.

title: Testing a New Approach to AI, Can Adaptive Computation Make Intelligence cheaper

blurb: I'm building, testing and researching an experimental AI architecture that aims to make AI systems more efficient computationally, basically making it cheaper
description:
### Project summary

I'm developing ACS(Adaptive Computational Substrate) which is an experimental AI architecture completely different from LLMs. Im currently investigating whether intelligence can be made more computationally efficient through adaptive allocation and reuse of computation  

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The primary goal is to determine whether adaptive computation and reusable computational structures can improve the efficiency of AI systems without significantly compromising task performance.  
Although this is a bold claim, i think it could POTENTIALLY become more mainstream as the use-cases increase for ACS.  
The project currently has 4 objectives:  
1\. Develop the architecture  
2\. Establish rigourous baselines  
3\. Measure efficiency  
4\. Publish findings  
  
I will proceed through implementation, controlled experimentation, failure analysis, and independent evaluation. The research will be guided by falsifiable hypotheses rather than assuming that the proposed architecture is superior since that is a more far fetched goal which is only viable if this whole thing works out.  

### How will you know it worked?

As mentioned in one of the objectives, success will be determined by measuring performance against established baselines.  
I'll measure:  
1\. Task success and correctness  
2\. Total model and tool costs  
3\. completion time  
4\. Number of failed attempts and retries  
5\. performance on repeated tasks versus unfamiliar tasks  
  
### How will this funding be used?

I am seeking 89000 USD for a 12 month independent research program.  
Due to circumstances i dont have a place to live currently so i will try to allocate 2500USD per month to living expenses which adds up to 30000 USD.  
9000 USD for Maintaining the Infrastructure and Software  
10000 USD contingency  
30000 USD for compute, research and model APIs  
The initial experiments and prototypes will be expensive but this is necessary to actually establish a fully working model and prove that costs can be cut and intelligence can be made cheaper using ACS  

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I have a potential collaborator residing in another country who has agreed to help me with ACS if i can provide proof of this being a viable product.  
  
I am at an early stage of research, and I do not yet have a track record of published AI research or demonstrated efficiency improvements from ACS. My current contribution is the initial implementation and the research direction.

The next phase will require more rigorous experimental design, comparisons against existing approaches, and independent evaluation. I intend to make the results available for scrutiny rather than rely on claims about the architecture's potential.  
  
I can promise a working public prototype in around 2-5 weeks after receiving the minimum funding needed for ACS  

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

If the project fails, I expect to produce a documented evaluation identifying which hypotheses were unsupported, which components introduced unnecessary overhead, and under what conditions adaptive computation was ineffective.

That outcome would help prevent further investment in an architecture that does not offer meaningful advantages. It could also identify narrower applications where the approach remains useful.

The project is designed to produce an informative result even if the original hypothesis is wrong.  

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

I have only raised about 2000 USD from my University proffessors to aid my research, due to my personal circumstances ill be starting to fully focus on this full time and have a working model ready by or before April 2027

title: Studying AI in governance within a simplistic simulated world
creator: bacf06ea-bfb3-4f27-b3c3-b40c2216ebbe
blurb: Studying the thought process and capabilities of AI models in governance within the simplified world of world box
description:
### Project summary

This project aims to modify the popular simulation game known as worldbox to be able to host two or more AI models e.g Claude,chat gpt etc and give them full control of a single Kingdom within world box. 

The purpose for the study is to test the thought process and actions of different AI models when giving priority of a single demographic rather than the entire world population as a whole, similarly it's also tests how AI models react and make decisions based on the cultures and existing practices of the people the govern within the simulation. 

This project idea came about from my belief that one of the eventual ends of AI technology would be a future where AI governs the entire world but it is also my personal belief that before this can happen AI will first govern individual countries and people's each with their own geographical issues and cultures. 

While worldbox is a simple simulation I believe it would be the ideal bases to use for this project as it is in its earliest stage and world box already possesses a large field of ideological practices for kingdoms within the game and as such can be used effectively to help produce feasible results in the early stages while being cost effective.  

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Since this is the exploratory stage the project has three goals which are: 

. To successfully modify world box to be able to host AI models to govern individual kingdoms 

. To have these AI models manage the policies and actions of their kingdoms through "trade, diplomacy, military strength and warfare. As well as monitoring how the react to the various cultures within world box i.e how would an AI model with a kingdom of xenophiles( accepting of other races) interact with a xenophobic nation.

. To obtain quantifiable data on the third process and actions of this AI models in order to confirm whether the research deserve more funding and deeper exploration or whether AI has not yet reached a point to govern a nation fully.

  
### How will you know it worked?

Due to the broad nature of this research a few of the ways to identify that the research has failed would be: 

. If the AI models make repetitive decisions rather than evolving decisions based on the situation 

. If multiple AI models continue to make repetitive decisions when given different cultures or geographical advantages i.e if a kingdom with scarce resources continues to make the same decisions as a kingdom with multiple resources despite not having the capacity so carry out this decisions. 

. If the actions of the AI model bring about the collapse of the nation the govern or lead to rebellions  

### How will this funding be used?

It will be used to:

.Hire a software developer: $8,250 bridge setup, mod configuration, multi-model agent loop, logging layer: 110 hrs @ $75/hr

.Hardware/materials: $700

.Data analysis will be handed by myself this includes dataset construction, quantitative + qualitative analysis, conclusions.

.LLM API costs: $2,200

.Margin of error: $4000

Total: $16,500  

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

For now I am the only member of the research but I hope to recruit other members to help me with the research. I hope to recruit or hire someone to work on the software development aspects and for that purpose I have devoted a large amount of the budget to fulfill whatever cost this may entail but I myself am a student of political science and a professionally certified data analyst and I will be taking care of whatever aspects involve data analysis as well as the eventual creation of the research work which will be made public.  

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

  
The most likely cause if the project should fail would be: 

. Inability to properly host the AI models for the simulation. 

. Lack of funding to provide proper materials to host the project 

. AI models making repetitive decisions regarding the simulation 

. AI models failing to govern their kingdoms within a simplified world which would prove that they are unable to govern a real one. 

The most likely outcome for what would happen if the research were to fail would be: 

. It would hopefully point out issues with AI thought processes that would help future researchers in the aim to study AI as an option in governance

. In the event that my research fails I would still make public all that I did to enjoy success and where I run into issues so that any and all future researchers could make reference of my work in order to avoid certain mistakes
