The total amount that we aim to race is around 16,500 but we applied to several places so any amount over $500 is considered a success in debate to raise money to fund this Grant.

title: Preference-label noise in small-model DPO: a reproducibility pilot
creator: 6d43d878-ea1c-498e-ba91-eb03432755bb
blurb: Up to $500 of GPU compute for controlled 0/10/20% label-noise comparisons, with public code, measured costs and negative results.
description:
### Project summary

I propose a small, public reproducibility study of how random preference-label noise affects Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) on an approximately 1.5B–3B open model. This is proposal-stage independent work, not a claim of a novel method or a demonstrated reduction in frontier AI risk.

What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Compare 0%, 10% and 20% random flips of training preference labels while holding a clean evaluation set and training budgets fixed. Start by selecting appropriately licensed public weights and preference data and profiling a tiny baseline. The measured memory and runtime will determine model/data size, sequence length and feasible repetitions. Run up to three seeds if resources permit; publish any scope reductions. Main experimental work is planned over 6–8 weeks after access is available.

How will you know it worked?

Success means releasing an auditable experiment: exact configurations, seeds and noise-injection procedure; held-out results across the noise conditions; measured GPU consumption; and a write-up stating uncertainty and limitations. A null or inconclusive result still counts as a useful output if it is reproducible. I do not promise improved model quality or claim that this small test establishes broad safety conclusions.

How will this funding be used?

Up to $500 for compute only: a provisional $50 profiling stage, $350 for controlled training comparisons, and $100 for fixed held-out evaluation/reproducibility reruns. These are spending ceilings, not measured quotes. The $500 supports only the experiments that measured costs allow. No salary, hardware purchase or travel is requested. I will reduce the scope rather than incur unapproved costs. Other applications are pending; any award will be disclosed and no experiment will be double funded.

Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am Anjan Bhanuprakash, a recent graduate based in India, working independently with no current enrollment, university/lab affiliation or registered company. I have used Qwen and Gemma and received a bronze medal in Kaggriculture on Kaggle. Public profiles: <https://github.com/anjan672> ; <https://www.linkedin.com/in/anjan-b-35a884295/> ; <https://www.kaggle.com/anjan4646/competitions> . These are general profiles, not an existing DPO project repo. No DPO demo, completed results or publications are claimed.

What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The model or training stack may not fit the available GPU, runtime may exceed the provisional budget, or the small study may be too noisy to show a meaningful difference. Profiling comes first so a smaller model, data subset or fewer seeds can be used. I will publish feasibility limits and negative findings rather than overstate an effect. Synthetic random flips are only a narrow proxy for preference-data errors and do not represent all real annotation noise.

How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

I have received no grant or sponsorship funding in the past 12 months ($0; no funding sources). Other funding applications are pending, with no awards confirmed. I will disclose any award and avoid double funding the same experiment.

Preparation note: this proposal was drafted with AI assistance from applicant-provided facts and the approved project scope. No experimental results have been generated or claimed.

title: Evidence and human oversight in institutional AI use in Pakistan
creator: 8e011fe6-7e6b-493f-b1e6-5d2c424e2a51
blurb: A six week discovery project using synthetic examples, practitioner interviews and a public review checklist.
description:
### Project summary

I am Ammara Aftab, founder and Chairperson of Pro AI Global in Karachi, Pakistan. I am seeking USD 2,500 for a six week exploratory project examining evidence quality and meaningful human review in one institutional AI document analysis workflow. The project would produce a public research brief, synthetic examples and a practical review checklist. It is a small discovery project, not a deployed system, a validated safety intervention or a claim of national impact.

What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The question is whether a simple review process can help institutional practitioners identify unsupported claims, unclear source provenance and situations requiring escalation when using AI generated document summaries. The first task is to review existing resources and determine whether a new checklist would add anything useful. I would narrow the project to one workflow before developing materials.

Week one would review relevant literature and existing guidance. Weeks two and three would seek up to eight consented adult practitioner or expert interviews about review needs. Weeks four and five would develop synthetic examples and a prototype checklist, seeking independent expert criticism where available. Week six would produce a public brief describing the evidence, limitations and whether further work appears justified. These are proposed activities, not completed research.

No institutional partner, interview access, confidential dataset or deployment permission is secured. Recruitment and any pilot would require appropriate consent and agreement. I would not collect confidential institutional documents or use the work to make consequential decisions about patients, learners, employees or other individuals. Public outputs would exclude identifiable interview material unless explicitly authorised. If access is insufficient, the output would explain that limitation rather than invent findings.

How will you know it worked?

Success would mean a clearly scoped question, a documented review of existing resources, transparent synthetic examples, a checklist that has received critical feedback where feasible, and an accessible brief distinguishing findings from assumptions. I would report what was actually completed, whether practitioners found the materials understandable, and whether existing guidance already meets the need. Interview counts alone would not establish improved safety. The project could reasonably conclude that a new intervention is unnecessary or that further research should take a different direction.

The possible connection to longer term AI risk is through institutions retaining the capacity to question and oversee increasingly capable systems. That connection is indirect and uncertain. I do not claim that this study would measure or demonstrate a reduction in catastrophic risk, nor do I claim technical alignment expertise.

How will this funding be used?

The proposed budget is USD 2,500: 1,500 for research and writing time; 300 for interview coordination, transcription and accessibility; 300 for independent expert review if engaged; 200 for tools, connectivity and research access; and 200 for editing and accessible publication. These are estimates, not incurred costs or signed contracts. Funding would reserve research time and support criticism beyond my own perspective. Without funding, I would explore a narrower literature review alongside existing work.

The work would begin after funding, lawful payment arrangements and any necessary ethics or institutional requirements are agreed. The six week schedule is provisional. I would agree an appropriate scope and reporting arrangements before accepting support. The intended public outputs would be available without a paid training requirement; this request is not for marketing or routine company operations.

Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I would lead the proposed research. No additional researcher or external expert is currently committed. I hold an MA in Applied Statistics from the University of Karachi and worked as Principal AI Research and Strategist at MEGNUS from January 2020 to December 2023\. I founded Pro AI Global in January 2023 and currently lead responsible AI education, institutional readiness and executive education work.

Supplied Government of Sindh acknowledgement letters document AI training in 2025 and 2026, including 101 newly inducted officers and a separate senior leadership audience in 2026\. Training through ORIC LUMHS engaged academic and medical professionals. I also serve as AI and Innovation Chair in Rotary District 3271, with reappointment documented for 2026/27\. These are practitioner and communication strengths, not evidence that I have already completed a comparable empirical research project.

Professional profile: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ammaraaftab/

Organisation: https://proaiglobal.com/

What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The main risks are limited interview access, duplicating existing guidance, an overly broad initial question, insufficient independent review and weak relevance to the most important AI governance problems. I would mitigate these by reviewing existing work first, narrowing the scope, using synthetic material and seeking criticism before recommending further investment. If recruitment or added value is inadequate, the brief would report that openly. No favourable outcome, partnership, publication acceptance or downstream adoption is promised.

How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

No award has been received for this project. Pro AI Global has received no outside investment, as confirmed by the applicant representative. Existing commercial income is separate from grant funding and is not described here as research funding.

The same USD 2,500 exploratory proposal is pending with BlueDot Rapid Grants, the Transformative AI Fund, GTR AI Safety Fund and the Foresight Human Empowerment research grant programme. This Manifund request is an alternative source for the same budget, not an additional USD 2,500 to spend on the same costs. Any award or material status change would be disclosed promptly, and duplicate funding would not be accepted. Related fellowship and research applications are also pending; any overlap in time, budget or outputs would be disclosed and resolved before acceptance. No fellowship selection or grant award is claimed.

title: Wordsmith Bench: Keeping Authors in Control of AI Editors
creator: 63d408ef-135f-407a-b5ae-b0d9145b38f2
blurb: Open tests of editorial judgment, harmful interventions and author control.
description:
### Project summary

An AI editor can make a sentence more conventional while making the book worse. The difficult question is whether it has found a mistake, encountered a deliberate choice, or failed to understand something original.

We are building Wordsmith Bench to make that distinction testable. Our ambition is to make judgment as scalable as generation while authors retain authority over their work. This grant funds a public benchmark of useful corrections, harmful interventions and decisions an AI should return to the author, together with a working demonstration of those controls.

We bring a live editorial system, a [public Model Bench pilot](https://wordsmith.page/benchmark/models), and an assembled group of literary and technical contributors. By 16 October 2026, Wordsmith had processed more than six million words across more than 400 pieces of writing. Our current benchmark uses AI judges. The next step is independent human calibration, rigorous controls and an open release that anyone can inspect and rerun.

US$36,820 funds 16 weeks: six rights-cleared works, 360 editorial decision cases, two independent readers, controlled originality experiments, three competing editorial-control policies and a 12-author exploratory study. A US$26,820 minimum funds a complete smaller version with four works, 240 cases and eight authors. Both versions release the code, licensed material, annotations, prompts and results, including failures.

The immediate public benefit is better evidence about AI editors. The larger ambition is to establish a practical way to test whether AI strengthens a person's judgment while respecting choices it does not fully understand.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

We want authors, editors and researchers to be able to ask three concrete questions of an AI system: does it find real problems, does it damage defensible choices, and does it know when to ask?

Wordsmith is building an AI-native publishing house, with the mission of giving every writer access to the capabilities of a publishing institution. Editorial judgment underpins that mission. This project makes part of that work public: a reproducible evaluation that competing tools and independent researchers can use without buying Wordsmith.

**1\. Build a human-calibrated editorial decision set.**

At the target budget, we will assemble six long-form works and 360 fixed candidate interventions, balanced across craft, line editing and polish. Cases will include actionable errors, defensible stylistic choices and decisions whose merits depend on author intent. Candidate interventions from multiple systems will be anonymised. Two independent readers will assess the same candidates with access to the relevant work and intent evidence. An editorial lead will calibrate the rubric and record adjudication, while preserving unresolved disagreement.

Four works will support development and two will remain held out until the methods, prompts and control policies are frozen. A published founder-owned work may support development. The holdout will use newly licensed unpublished material with explicit public-release rights. We will report contamination checks without claiming they prove a text was absent from model training.

This creates a test of decisions within whole works, rather than a competition to produce the most feedback. Agreement with our own editor, an AI judge's preference or an author's click on Accept will not establish correctness.

**2\. Test whether direct exposure reveals something a description misses.**

Our originality work asks whether a model learns something from encountering a work that it cannot recover from a strong description of it. A reliable difference could help identify deliberate structures that generic editing rules would mistake for errors. On four passages per work, we will compare imitation from a description, a sample elsewhere in the work and the rest of the book with the target passage removed.

We will use repeated generations, separate generator and judge model families, stronger descriptions, matched conventional rewrites, shuffled passages and human checks. These controls distinguish a possible response to form from factual recall, recognisable mannerisms or judge preference. A surprising sentence alone is not evidence of literary merit.

We already have informal experiments and a revised preregistration. Early controls exposed a judge that rewarded access to content even when form was flattened or scrambled. Stronger descriptions also reduced some apparent gaps. The grant lets us test the revised method across independent works. The description-gap signal will influence editorial control only if it survives its controls and improves decisions against the human annotations.

**3\. Demonstrate useful author control.**

We will compare three policies on the same fixed candidate interventions: ordinary recommendations, abstention when uncertain, and an intent-aware policy that protects explicit author constraints and asks about contested choices. The demonstration will show what each policy recommends, defers or declines, with an explanation an author can challenge. All edits remain reversible and require author approval.

The primary comparison measures harmful interventions alongside recall of independently labelled actionable errors. We will also report abstention, reader disagreement and review time. A system that avoids every decision cannot pass by doing nothing. Our practical target is a 25% relative reduction in harmful interventions against ordinary recommendations, with no more than a five-percentage-point loss in useful-error recall on the held-out works. This is a research target, not an existing result or a promised outcome.

A counterbalanced exploratory study with 12 authors will test whether people can understand and challenge the recommendations on licensed passages. A fresh passage completed without AI will probe learning rather than acceptance alone. The study will publish consented, de-identified data and cannot support a population-level effectiveness claim.

**Delivery over 16 weeks**

* **Weeks 1-4.** Protocol, rights register, rubric and open harness skeleton. Formalise paid contributor work packages and appoint independent readers. Time a 30-case calibration pilot before committing the remaining annotation budget.
* **Weeks 5-8.** Development set, independent annotations and controlled description-gap results. Freeze model versions, prompts and analysis. Publish whether the proposed signal survives its controls.
* **Weeks 9-12.** Working control demonstration and frozen held-out evaluation. Publish useful-error recall, harmful interventions, disagreement and uncertainty by work.
* **Weeks 13-16.** Author study, complete open release and final report. A reader who did not build the harness will reproduce a selected result from the release instructions. Publish actual spending against this budget.

The minimum budget preserves all three workstreams, both independent readers and two held-out works. It reduces development to two works, the complete decision set to 240 cases and the author study to eight participants. Both versions treat the works as a small pilot, rather than treating hundreds of decisions as independent samples of literature. Results will include raw counts and uncertainty at the work level.

**Public release and longer-term use**

New funded code will be released under Apache-2.0\. Documentation, annotations and the commissioned or expressly licensed corpus will use CC BY 4.0\. The release will include the prompts, rubrics, analysis, model settings and permitted run outputs needed to reproduce the reported results. Model routes will be chosen with redistribution terms in mind. An undisclosed scoring prompt, private manuscript or proprietary Wordsmith service cannot be a necessary dependency of a funded result.

We want this to become a reference test that can be rerun as models change. The first release will provide instructions for adding new systems and works. Over the following years, our ambition is independent replications and separately validated extensions into translation and substantive nonfiction. Those extensions require new funding and expertise. Human control in other domains is a research hypothesis to investigate, not an impact already demonstrated by this project.

### How will you know it worked?

By week 16, another team should be able to reproduce a reported result using the public release, without access to Wordsmith's private systems. We will have released the protocol, licensed corpus, independent annotations, evaluation code, prompts, model settings, control demonstration and final analysis. A reader who did not build the harness will reproduce a selected result from the release instructions.

We will separately report whether the control policy achieves our practical target: at least 25% fewer harmful interventions relative to ordinary recommendations, with no more than a five-percentage-point loss in useful-error recall on the held-out works. The analysis will include counts, disagreement and uncertainty by work. The author study will examine comprehension, challenges to advice, review time and performance on a fresh passage without AI.

A positive description-gap result is not a condition for success. A complete benchmark and a reproducible negative result still help others avoid misleading evaluations. Failure to release the funded work or dependence on undisclosed private components would mean we had not delivered the public benefit.

### How will this funding be used?

The binding constraint is sustained paid time for the contributors already drawn to this work. Funding gives them defined responsibilities, blocks of working time and a common release schedule across engineering, experimental design, literary calibration and public release. Independent readers are budgeted separately from the people building the evaluation.

All amounts are in US dollars. Quantities and rates are planning estimates to be agreed before work starts.

* **Research engineering.** Minimum 240 hours x $40 = $9,600\. Target 320 hours x $40 = $12,800.
* **Evaluation methods and analysis.** Minimum 120 hours x $45 = $5,400\. Target 160 hours x $45 = $7,200.
* **Literary calibration.** Minimum 80 hours x $40 = $3,200\. Target 100 hours x $40 = $4,000.
* **Two independent readers, combined.** Minimum 88 hours x $50 = $4,400\. Target 120 hours x $50 = $6,000.
* **Author-study compensation.** Minimum 8 authors x 1.5 hours x $40 = $480\. Target 12 authors x 1.5 hours x $40 = $720.
* **Corpus licence honoraria.** Minimum 4 works x $150 = $600\. Target 6 works x $150 = $900.
* **Model APIs and compute.** Minimum 4 work blocks x $300 = $1,200\. Target 4 work blocks x $600 = $2,400.
* **Documentation and replication.** Minimum 36 hours x $35 = $1,260\. Target 48 hours x $35 = $1,680.
* **Grant administration.** Minimum 17 hours x $40 = $680\. Target 28 hours x $40 = $1,120.
* **Total.** Minimum $26,820\. Target $36,820.

The additional $10,000 buys two more works, 120 more decision cases, four more author-study participants, and the engineering and review time to support them. The larger development set gives us more opportunities to reject a misleading method before opening the holdout. At either level, both held-out works and the open release remain funded.

The independent-reader allocation includes full-work context, scoring and adjudication. The first month's timed pilot will test whether the workload fits. Licence honoraria assume willing partners and adequate release rights. Rights are not yet secured. We will replace material or agree a smaller scope before incurring later costs if the required permissions or reader capacity cannot be obtained within budget.

AI will help scaffold code, generate candidate interventions and controls, check citation spans and organise run records. Caching and staged runs will limit long-context API costs. Human literary assessment remains paid work. Applicable credits will reduce the cash claim; their face value will not be counted as cash expenditure.

Euwyn will contribute approximately three hours per week of project oversight and Yash two hours of technical oversight in kind for 16 weeks. The grant pays for additional open research work, documentation and administration. It includes no retrospective founder salary, travel, advertising, customer acquisition or routine commercial feature development. Contract rates are budget caps, subject to agreement on the scope and applicable costs. There is no additional institutional overhead.

Between the minimum and target, we will first protect complete works, two independent assessments and the held-out comparison, then add development material and paid analysis time. We will publish the exact scope and revised line items before spending. We will not expand beyond the target without a separately costed public extension and agreement with the relevant funders.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

We have already attracted an A+ group of contributors on belief and goodwill: an experienced writer-editor and writing-community leader, narrative researchers, and AI product engineers. They bring the literary craft, research and systems expertise needed to make editorial judgment testable. Funding turns that existing collaboration into structured paid work with clear ownership and a shared delivery schedule.

**Euwyn Goh, co-founder and project lead.** I spent four years writing and self-publishing _After Nihilism_. Assembling the editing, production and publication process myself led to Wordsmith. I lead product, editorial direction and operations. Previously, I led GTM and business operations at Gnosis Business and built Hansa's accelerator. For this project, I will lead the research questions, author relationships, study operations and public accountability. [Profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/euwyng)

**Yash Wanvari, co-founder and technical lead.** Yash built Wordsmith end to end. He previously spent five years at CommerceIQ, from its Series A period through its growth into a unicorn, leading engineering pods. He will direct the evaluation architecture, reproducible experiments and engineering execution. [Profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yash-wanvari)

Our existing contributors cover editorial craft and calibration, narrative structure and meaning, and AI architecture and evaluation. The editorial expertise includes twenty years of writing and editing and leadership within a writing community. Research contributors bring work across narrative systems, theoretical computer science and AI. Their contributions have already shaped the product and the originality experiments. At award, we will finalise paid work packages across this group and appoint two independent readers for the study.

We have shipped a live manuscript-scale editorial product and [Wordsmith Model Bench](https://wordsmith.page/benchmark/models), which compares craft, line editing and polish. The current pilot requires feedback to cite the text, penalises harmful interventions, uses judges from multiple providers and reports uncertainty. It explicitly identifies the missing human calibration that this proposal funds.

We also bring the description-gap experiments and v0.4 preregistration. The early failures changed our protocol before we expanded it. That is the standard we will carry into the funded work: publish the evidence, test interpretations against controls and let independent assessment overturn our preferred result.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

**The proposed originality signal may measure the wrong thing.** A gap can reflect recall, weak descriptions or a judge's taste. We will publish the controlled result, including a failure to find the proposed effect. The editorial-control comparison can proceed using explicit intent and calibrated uncertainty. A positive description-gap result is not required for the public benchmark to be useful.

**Readers may disagree, or the control policy may protect voice by missing real errors.** We will preserve disagreement labels and report harmful interventions jointly with useful-error recall. If the policy fails that comparison, we will publish where it fails. We will not present a small set of books as a universal literary standard or rank authors by quality.

**Rights or review time may constrain the corpus.** The month-one rights and timing gate comes before the main spend. Permission to process a manuscript does not permit its publication. Private customer manuscripts and private correspondence will not enter the public release. Material must be founder-owned, commissioned or explicitly licensed for the planned open distribution. If the proposed scope is infeasible, we will agree a smaller deliverable and budget with funders before proceeding.

**Our commercial incentives could distort the evaluation.** Wordsmith may benefit from the research, so independent readers will assess anonymised candidates and the protocol will be frozen before held-out testing. Funded artifacts will be usable by competitors. We will publish unfavourable results and separate the new public work from existing commercial code and data in a project register.

The most likely disappointing outcome is a useful small benchmark and a negative result on the proposed signal or control policy. That would still reveal which evaluation shortcuts fail and provide independently assessed cases for future work. The project fails its public purpose if its claims cannot be reproduced or its outputs remain private. We will prioritise the complete open release over a favourable headline.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

Wordsmith is bootstrapped. We have not received a cash research grant for the work proposed here. Customer payments support the commercial product and publishing work; they are separate from research fundraising.

In-kind company support includes US$5,000 in OpenAI API credits awarded in June 2026 and US$25,000 in Google Cloud credits awarded in August 2026\. These are original award amounts, not remaining balances or cash in the bank. Wordsmith was also selected for an ElevenLabs startup grant in October; that offer provides service credits and is not cash for this study. Any usable, unspent credits applied to this project will reduce its cash costs.

We have two pending research applications with overlapping scope: Foresight, submitted in October for US$40,000 with a US$30,000 reduced version, and Lightcone Commons, submitted in August for a broader phased programme at US$150,000 with a US$50,000 minimum. Neither is an award or committed revenue in this budget. The Manifund budget removes the Foresight-specific US$3,180 Node visit from both versions.

This is an alternative or coordinated source of support for the public research, not an additional claim on costs funded elsewhere. We will disclose any award before accepting overlapping support, allocate each cost to one funder and revise the public fundraising need. If another award fully covers this scope, we will reduce or close this request. Any distinct extension would need a new scope, budget and funder agreement.

title: Max — a fully interpretable, air-gapped approach to general agency
creator: 39f4e438-3642-4d9b-80fc-affc15e1d80d
blurb: An offline AI agent whose every step is a readable rule — interpretability and containment built in, tested on ARC-AGI-3.
description:
### Project summary

Max is an AI agent built on a single bet: that general reasoning can be made fully transparent. Instead of opaque neural weights, every capability Max has is an explicit, human-readable rule, so each decision can be traced to a specific principle, and the effect of each principle can be measured by switching it off. Max runs entirely offline on one local machine, with containment and operator goal-approval built in from the start, and its progress is measured on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark. I’m an independent researcher building it solo.  

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Frontier AI is powerful but opaque — we can’t read why a model does what it does. Max is the opposite approach: an agent assembled entirely from explicit, general principles. Every choice traces back to a named rule, nothing is hard-coded to a specific puzzle, and each capability has to earn its place as a genuinely general principle rather than a shortcut.

I build it under a strict test-first discipline. Before writing a capability I write tests for it — hundreds of them — and I replay recorded episodes through the agent to check its behaviour. No capability is accepted unless there’s a test that fails without it, which keeps the whole system honest and makes any regression visible.

Safety is structural, not added afterwards. Max runs on one local machine, fully offline, with no network access at all. Containment is physical: the agent is fed information only through physical media by me, the operator, and I approve its goals and sub-goals. By design it cannot choose harmful means, cannot copy itself, cannot alter its own rules or checks, and must stop on command.

The longer-term reason to pursue transparent general reasoning is the problems it could eventually help with — above all scientific and medical discovery. An agent that can learn and reason in genuinely new situations, and whose every step a human can read and check, is the kind of tool that could one day help accelerate research into disease. That is exactly why it must be built safely and transparently from the ground up. This grant funds the concrete first step toward that — not a medical result, but the trustworthy reasoning engine such work would depend on.  

### How will you know it worked?

For this stage, success means:

* Measurably better results on ARC-AGI-3 than today — more tasks and levels solved, reported as clear before/after numbers.
* A capability-test suite that keeps growing and stays green, so every new ability is backed by a test that fails without it.
* A public write-up of the method, the full set of principles, and the results, detailed enough that others can inspect and critique it.
* Demonstrable safety properties: every decision traceable to a rule, and the containment design holding throughout.

If the numbers don’t improve but the method and negative results are clearly documented, that is still a real, shareable outcome.  

### How will this funding be used?

* A local research workstation. The work is currently bottlenecked on hardware: \~$7,200 (50,000 DKK).
* A part-time stipend for me for 12 months, so I can work on Max consistently: \~$1,600/month gross (roughly $1,000/month after Danish tax), \~$19,200 total.

Target: \~$26,500\. Minimum to keep going: \~$7,200 (the workstation alone).

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I’m an independent, self-taught researcher working on this solo. My track record is the artifact itself: a working agent developed under a disciplined test-first regime, a growing suite of capability tests, measured results on ARC-AGI-3, and an explicit safety architecture (physical containment, operator approval, and immutable self-rules). I’m offering the method and the results for open scrutiny.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The most likely failure is that the first-principles approach plateaus before reaching human-level generality on ARC-AGI-3\. As a solo project it also carries key-person risk. But even then the work produces value: a documented, reproducible method, honest benchmark numbers, and a concrete demonstration of an interpretable, contained design — results that are useful to others whether or not the capability goal is reached.  

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

None — the project has been entirely self-funded so far.

title: Help Me Keep My AI Memory Research in the Conference
creator: f2e65f25-3e59-4a8b-9ef8-e69e1e48afe0
blurb: My paper was accepted to SIAI 2026. I’m currently homeless & raising $500 to cover the registration and help replace the 2017 MacBook I use to do the work.
description:
I’m an independent AI builder and researcher in Wisconsin. I don’t work for a university or a lab. Most of what I’ve done has just come from being curious about AI companions, building things, testing ideas, and trying to document what I’m finding as I go.

One of the problems I got interested in was memory. If an AI companion remembers something wrong about a person and they correct it, does that correction actually stick? Does it get used later, or does the system keep falling back to the old information?

I ended up writing a short paper about that called _Tracing Corrections Through AI Companion Memory: A Practical Evaluation Protocol and Exploratory Case Study._

It got accepted to SIAI 2026, the International Conference on the Social Impact of AI, which is happening November 13–14 in Boston.

The part I’m stuck on now is the registration fee.

They require at least one author to register by October 25 or the paper gets dropped from the proceedings. The author registration is $150\. I asked if they could waive it because of my financial situation, but they declined.

I’m currently homeless, so $150 is not something I can just pull together right now.

This fund has a $500 minimum, so I want to be upfront about that instead of trying to make it sound like the conference itself costs $500.

The first $150 would go directly to the SIAI registration so the paper stays in the conference.

Any access would go toward replacing the computer I’m using for this work. I’m still doing basically everything on a 2017 MacBook Air. Coding, testing AI systems, writing, research, running my website, all of it. It still works, but I’ve definitely pushed it pretty far.

I’m not asking for money to travel to Boston. If I can’t make the trip, I can present virtually.

I also try to keep my work public. I’ve built open-source tools around AI memory evaluation and companion portability, and I post research work here:

<https://troymaya.com/research/>

If this gets funded, I’ll post the registration receipt, and once the paper is published I’ll share that too. I’ll also be transparent about what happens with the rest of the money.

I’m basically just trying to keep something I already worked hard enough to get accepted from getting stopped at the last step because I can’t afford the registration.
